title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Phoenix, AZ: 6-Day Course
description: AWS CWI exam prep for Phoenix: a six-day course online or at your site, shaped by chip fab, data centre and structural steel construction in the Valley.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Phoenix: Six Days for Fab, Data Centre and Steel Inspectors
html:
The Phoenix metro has turned into one of the largest industrial construction markets in the country, and the reason is easy to see from the freeways: semiconductor fabrication plants in north Phoenix and Chandler, data centre campuses across the East and West Valley, and the structural steel, process piping and utility work that comes with both. Every one of those projects needs people who can check welds against a code and put their name on the result. Atlantis NDT's six-day course for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector exam is aimed at welders, pipefitters, QC technicians, NDT technicians and engineers in the Valley who want to sit the AWS CWI exam. Candidates on their own take it online, with a structured plan, materials, original practice questions and an instructor available for questions. A contractor or fabricator preparing a crew can book the full programme at its own yard, shop or project office. Ask for a Phoenix quote to begin.

Before you plan around the course, understand who does what. AWS owns the CWI exam from application to score report and awards the certification to those who pass and qualify. Atlantis's contribution is the preparation; it does not grant any certification, never sees an exam paper, and is not approved or endorsed by AWS. Every practice question in the course is an Atlantis original based on AWS's published subject areas.

Semiconductor fabs and the welding behind them

TSMC's Arizona campus in Phoenix covers more than 1,100 acres. According to ENR's July 2026 report, the first fab there reached high-volume production in late 2024, the second has finished construction ahead of 3-nanometer production planned for 2027, and the third broke ground in 2025. The same report says the campus plan now allows for ten fabs, two advanced packaging plants and a research centre. In Chandler, Intel's Ocotillo campus added Fabs 52 and 62, whose construction began in 2022. Together those projects have pulled a large construction workforce into the Valley and will keep generating expansion, retrofit and tool-install work for years.

A fab is a welding inspection project of several kinds at once. The building itself is heavy structural steel, welded and erected to AWS D1.1, with special inspection under the building code. Under and around the cleanrooms sits a dense web of process piping: ultra-high-purity stainless steel lines for gases and chemicals, often joined by orbital gas tungsten arc welding, plus acid waste, solvent, exhaust and utility systems. Much of that piping is designed to ASME B31.3, whose high-purity fluid service rules sit in a chapter of their own, and owners often add requirements from ASME BPE or their own specifications on weld color, bead profile and internal surface condition. Inspectors on high-purity work examine coupons and borescope images of the inside of orbital welds, check purge practice, and confirm that every weld log entry matches a qualified welder and procedure. Atlantis does not write or qualify those welding procedures; that remains with the owner and the piping contractor.

For a CWI candidate, the practical consequence is code choice. Most fab inspectors work in two worlds: D1.1 for the steel and B31.3 for the piping. Both are Part C options. Candidates heading for pipe and tool-install work usually do better with B31.3; those working for steel fabricators and special inspection agencies usually pick D1.1.

Data centre campuses across the Valley

The Phoenix area has also become a major data centre market. One early large project, Meta's campus in Mesa, began construction in 2021, and many more campuses have followed in the East Valley, the West Valley and the corridors around Goodyear and Buckeye. A data centre is less exotic than a fab but just as demanding on schedule. The work includes steel framing and roof structures, mechanical piping for chilled water and condenser systems, fuel piping for standby generators, and large electrical yards with welded steel supports.

Welding inspectors on these sites split their time between structural welds under D1.1 and piping welds under the project's mechanical specification, which commonly references ASME B31.1, B31.3 or B31.9 depending on the system. The owners are sophisticated buyers who expect complete documentation at turnover, so an inspector who keeps clean, traceable records is worth as much to the general contractor as one who spots defects quickly.

Structural steel, special inspection and the Arizona sun

Outside the mega-projects, the Valley's growth keeps structural steel shops, erectors and testing agencies busy with warehouses, hospitals, schools, parking structures and mid-rise towers. Valley cities adopt the International Building Code, each with its own amendments, and structural steel welding falls under the code's special inspection provisions. Each jurisdiction decides which credentials it accepts for structural welding special inspectors, so confirm the current requirement with the building department you will work under. Many agencies ask for the AWS CWI, an ICC certification, or both.

Heat changes the job here. Steel left in the summer sun can get too hot to touch, which affects interpass temperature control, primer and coating application, and the comfort and concentration of everyone on the deck. Low-hydrogen electrodes still need proper storage even in dry air. An inspector working in summer schedules early starts, carries water, and still has to measure and record interpass temperatures on heavy members where the procedure sets a maximum. That habit of measuring before judging is the core of Part B.

Mining, utilities and the rest of Arizona's welding work

Beyond the metro, Arizona is a major copper mining state, and mines and processing plants run constant repair and fabrication welding on haul-truck frames, shovels, crushers, conveyors, chutes, tanks and slurry piping. Utilities add power plant maintenance, transmission structures, water and wastewater projects, and natural gas distribution work overseen at the state level by the Arizona Corporation Commission's pipeline safety office. Those sectors hire welding inspectors too, often from the same pool of candidates who started on Phoenix construction projects. For context on inspection methods in these industries, see UT in steel and MT for fabrication.

Employers in the Valley that look for a CWI

  • Mechanical and process piping contractors on fab and data centre projects, which need inspectors for high-purity and utility piping.
  • Structural steel fabricators and erectors supplying fabs, data halls, warehouses and public buildings.
  • Special inspection and testing agencies retained by owners under the building code.
  • Owners' quality teams and construction managers on the large semiconductor and data centre programs, who verify contractor work.
  • Mining companies and their repair contractors, where repair welding on heavy equipment needs visual and procedural checks.
  • Utilities, water agencies and their engineering consultants on plant and pipeline work.

Where Phoenix candidates sit the AWS exam

The examination is in three parts, and AWS requires at least 72 percent on each. Part A, Fundamentals, covers welding processes, metallurgy, testing, symbols, procedure qualification documents, safety and inspection math in 150 questions. Part B, Practical, adds hands-on tasks to its 46 questions: candidates measure and judge weld samples with inspection tools and apply procedure and qualification records. Part C, Code Application, is an open-book paper of 50 to 65 questions on the code selected at application.

Parts A and C are computer-based and booked with Prometric after AWS accepts the application and sends an eligibility code; AWS says it has more than 100 Prometric centres in the US. Part B is different, and this is the main logistics point for Arizona. AWS gives the practical only at its own seminar locations, and no Arizona city is on its current list of US CWI seminar locations. The closest listed cities are Los Angeles and Denver, so most Valley candidates plan a short trip for Part B. Check aws.org for the current list and dates before booking travel.

How the six days fit a Phoenix schedule

The course plan is set out day by day on the national AWS CWI exam prep course page. The first day covers processes, joint design, symbols as drawn in AWS A2.4 and terms as defined in AWS A3.0. The second day covers metallurgy, mechanical testing, discontinuity causes, destructive and nondestructive testing, safety and inspector ethics. Day three trains the gauging and visual judgment that Part B tests. Day four keeps the candidate inside the Part C code book. The fifth runs timed mock exams for all three parts, followed by review. The sixth closes gaps and prepares the AWS application, the documents and the exam-day plan.

On a fab or data centre job, overtime and shift changes make fixed class times unrealistic, which is why the individual version is self-paced online: no start date, no scheduled sessions, and an instructor who answers questions when the candidate sends them. The employer version brings all six days to the contractor's or fabricator's own site. For a piping contractor, the third day can use the company's own weld coupons and gauges, and the fourth can concentrate on B31.3 if that is where the crew works. Atlantis does not supply replica kits and has no training facility in Arizona; the venue is always the employer's.

Between sessions, Valley candidates can drill testing topics with the free NDT practice tests and walk through inspection steps in the Practical NDT welding workshop. To see where candidates commonly fall short, read the CWI results breakdown by part.

AWS eligibility for Valley candidates

AWS sets eligibility in QC1, now listed as the 2016 edition with Amendment 1. It weighs schooling against years spent in welding-based work:

  • Bachelor's or higher in welding engineering or welding engineering technology: one year of experience.
  • Associate or higher in welding, engineering, engineering technology or physical science: two years.
  • Engineering or technical courses counting toward a welding bachelor's: three years.
  • Completed trade or vocational courses: four years.
  • High school diploma or an approved equivalent: five years.
  • Eighth-grade schooling: nine years. Less than eighth grade: twelve years.

Candidates submit an employment verification form backing up the experience, the AWS Visual Acuity Exam Form recording a passed vision examination, and photo identification that meets AWS's requirements. Pipefitters and orbital welders from fab projects should describe their work precisely, including the systems, materials and codes involved. AWS decides what qualifies, and a vague description makes that decision harder. The course's last day reviews the paperwork; the application, the vision examination and the AWS fees stay with the candidate. The guide to CWI requirements covers the rules in more depth.

Phoenix welding schools and the AWS Arizona Section

Arizona members belong to the AWS Arizona Section, which sits in AWS District 21. Section meetings are where Valley inspectors, educators, fabricators and suppliers meet, and they are a good place to find a recently certified CWI who will share how they prepared, which employers are hiring, and how local technical programs count toward recertification.

The Valley's welding schools are expanding with the construction boom. GateWay Community College in Phoenix offers welding certificates that include structural welding technologies and precision welding technologies. Mesa Community College offers a certificate of completion in welding. West-MEC has opened an adult welding technology program at its Buckeye campus in the West Valley. Graduates who go on to several years of structural, pipe or orbital welding build the kind of record that supports a CWI application, and an associate degree also shortens the experience AWS requires.

After the exam: keeping the CWI and adding NDT

AWS issues the CWI for nine years, with renewal due at year three and year six. Renewal asks you to confirm that you have not been away from practice or employment for more than two years in the preceding three. At nine years you recertify through one of the routes AWS lists, which include retaking Part B and documenting 80 professional development hours. Inspectors who stay in the field can later pursue Senior CWI, covered in the SCWI pathway article.

Fab, data centre and mining specifications frequently call for penetrant, magnetic particle or ultrasonic examination after visual acceptance, so many Valley CWIs add NDT methods. Atlantis's NDT courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A, which leaves certification to your employer and its written practice rather than to any course. Good next steps are VT Level 2 training, PT training and the NDT training options for Phoenix. Atlantis offers API 510, 570, 580 and 653 exam prep separately, as self-paced online courses. To compare the welding inspector and NDT routes, see how the CWI compares with API 577 and ASNT Level II. For field services rather than training, Atlantis offers weld inspection in Phoenix and penetrant testing in Phoenix; see also Phoenix inspection services.

Requesting a Phoenix quote

Tell us whether this is one person or a group, the current job and welding-based experience of each candidate, the Part C book you expect to use (D1.1 and B31.3 cover most Valley work), and when you want to sit the exam, keeping in mind the trip for Part B. For on-site delivery, add the site address, any badging or safety orientation the site requires, and whether a room, gauges and weld samples are available. AWS publishes its examination and seminar charges on aws.org, and the CWI exam budget calculator helps you account for travel to the Part B city. Send the Phoenix request; we reply within one business day.

Related pages: Los Angeles CWI prep and Denver CWI prep, the two nearest Part B cities, and Salt Lake City CWI prep.

faq.q: Can I take the CWI practical exam in Arizona?
faq.a: Not currently. AWS gives Part B only at its seminar locations, and no Arizona city is on its present US list. Los Angeles and Denver are the closest listed cities. Parts A and C can be taken at a Prometric centre in the Valley. Check aws.org, as the list changes.

faq.q: Which Part C code book fits semiconductor fab work?
faq.a: Piping and tool-install inspectors usually choose ASME B31.3, which includes high-purity fluid service rules. Inspectors on the building steel usually choose AWS D1.1. Both are on the current AWS list.

faq.q: Does the course cover orbital welding of high-purity piping?
faq.a: It covers the welding processes, discontinuities and code navigation that underpin that work, and an on-site group can focus the code day on B31.3. Owner-specific acceptance rules for weld color and internal profile still come from the project specification.

faq.q: Is the CWI accepted for special inspection in Phoenix?
faq.a: Each building department sets its own rules for structural welding special inspectors. Many accept the AWS CWI, an ICC certification or both. Confirm with the jurisdiction you will work under.

faq.q: Does Atlantis have a classroom in Phoenix?
faq.a: No. Individuals work online and send questions to an instructor; employers can bring the programme to their own premises.

faq.q: Is the course really six days?
faq.a: Yes, six days of content. Employer groups normally run them consecutively; online candidates spread them out to suit shifts and overtime.
AWS runs every part of the exam and grants the CWI. Atlantis prepares candidates for it, and the course carries no AWS approval or endorsement.

faq.q: How much experience do I need as a pipefitter with a high school diploma?
faq.a: AWS QC1 asks for five years of welding-based experience with a high school diploma or approved equivalent. AWS decides whether pipefitting duties count, so describe the welding-related work clearly.

faq.q: Can our piping contractor host the course at a fab project?
faq.a: Yes, subject to the site's access and safety rules. Send the number of candidates, their roles and the site's orientation requirements through the quote form, and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: What should I add after the CWI in Arizona?
faq.a: Visual and penetrant testing suit fab and stainless work well. Atlantis teaches both to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and your employer grants the certification. See NDT training for Phoenix.
